chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Ibn Maḥbūb, from al-Ḥasan ibn Ṣāliḥ al-Thawrī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
“When the water in the well reaches a kurr, nothing makes it impure.” I said: “And how much is a kurr?” He said: “Three spans and a half in its depth, by three spans and a half in its width.”

Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan said: We have already clarified that the ruling of wells differs from the ruling of ponds, and that wells become impure by what falls into them and are purified by drawing out some of their water, whether the water in them is little or abundant. The proper way to understand this report is that we carry it upon a form of taqiyyah, because it agrees particularly with the doctrine of some of the ʿAmmah; and its narrator is al-Ḥasan ibn Ṣāliḥ, and he is a Zaydī Butrī, whose uniquely transmitted reports are not acted upon.

key_terms.أَشْبَارٍ: spans, a hand-based unit of measurement
key_terms.التَّقِيَّةِ: dissimulation or precautionary conformity under certain circumstances
key_terms.الرَّكِيِّ: the well; here referring to well-water
key_terms.الْغُدْرَانِ: ponds or pools of standing water
key_terms.كُرًّا: the quantity of kurr, a legal volumetric measure relevant to impurity rulings

ai.seo_question: What does Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām say about kurr water in a well and whether it becomes impure?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the legal ruling of water in wells and the measurement of kurr as a threshold related to impurity. The accompanying statement of Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan explains that, in Shia jurisprudential treatment, this specific report is not followed as the operative ruling for wells and is understood in light of taqiyyah and narrator-based considerations.
